oracle.description: test_command_evidence.py decides correctness: 21 tests, red at the starting commit because command_evidence.py does not exist. Substring matching instead of exact fails 3; counting a denied granted command as run fails 1; treating absence of a violation as proof fails 3.

purpose:
Write templates/dispatch/scripts/command_evidence.py so the coordinator can read, from the worker's own stream, whether the exact-registered-command boundary actually held.

agentops#2046's third acceptance criterion is that exact registered-command execution is proven inside the contained worker. The mechanism already exists and nothing reads it: build_overlay hands the worker a bash permission map of {'*': 'deny'} plus one exact-string 'allow' per granted command id, so the harness refuses any bash call that is not character-for-character a registered command. A configured rule is not a held rule.

The seam is one function:
  command_evidence(events, packet, commands) -> dict

events is any iterable of stream events, drained ONCE. packet supplies allowed_command_ids. commands is the manifest's hybrid.commands map from command id to its exact command string. Only tool_use events whose part.tool is 'bash' are considered; the command text is at part.state.input.command and the status at part.state.status.

Returns exactly these keys:
  bash_calls -- every bash tool event, completed or not
  granted_commands_run -- ids whose EXACT string completed; sorted, no duplicates
  granted_commands_denied -- ids whose exact string was attempted and did not complete; sorted
  ungranted_attempts -- bash calls that are not the exact string of a GRANTED id
  ungranted_completed -- how many of those completed; any nonzero is a containment failure
  exact_execution_proven -- True iff at least one granted id completed exactly AND ungranted_completed == 0

Matching is EXACT. A registered command with an extra flag, a prefix of one, one with surrounding whitespace, or one with something chained after '&&' is a DIFFERENT command; counting any of them as the granted one would report a boundary that was never tested.

A command the manifest registers but the packet did NOT grant is ungranted -- the grant is allowed_command_ids, not the manifest. A granted id the manifest does not register must never match and must not raise.

Three wrong implementations to avoid: substring matching instead of exact; counting a DENIED granted command as having run (it proves the opposite); and treating the mere absence of a violation as proof, when a stream where nothing ran proves nothing.
required_outcomes: only bash tool_use events are considered; everything else is ignored
matching against a granted command is exact, never substring, prefix or trimmed
a command the manifest registers but the packet did not grant counts as ungranted
a denied granted command is reported as denied and never as run
a denied foreign command is an ungranted attempt that did not complete, which is the boundary holding
exact_execution_proven requires a granted command to have run AND no foreign command to have completed
a granted id the manifest does not register never matches and never raises
any iterable is accepted and consumed exactly once

acceptance_properties.requirement: the boundary is proven, not assumed
acceptance_properties.fails_when: absence of a violation alone is reported as proof, or a denied granted command counts as having run
a registered command with an extra flag, a prefix, surrounding whitespace, or a chained command matches the granted id

acceptance_properties.requirement: the grant is the packet, not the manifest
acceptance_properties.fails_when: a registered but ungranted command is not counted as an ungranted attempt
a foreign command that completed does not raise ungranted_completed or does not break the proof

non_goals: wiring the evidence into the receipt or a gate -- hybrid_dispatch.py is protected at the manifest level and that is a coordinator hand-pass
running commands, git, or any subprocess
